notes: Building and Industrial News, vol. 13 part 1 (Internet Archive buildingindustri1313cont), the 25 weekly issues from 7 January to 25 June 1913. The paper came out on Tuesdays until 20 May and on Wednesdays from 28 May. Same method as the later volumes of this source and the Building and Engineering News run that follows it: every numbered entry under Building Permit Applications and Building Contracts was taken from the djvu.xml OCR, East Bay headings set aside, and each San Francisco lot built from the block corner on the DPW street centrelines and compared with the sf-parcels shapes; a placement was accepted where the lot starts within two feet of a lot line of today (or the record names an unambiguous corner) and the roll year fits, and alterations were matched by printed street number in sf-eas-addresses where the roll dates the building before the work. The issues were dated from their covers ('Issued Weekly ... Thirteenth Year, No. N'). extract.py ran with BEN_LOOSE=1; item numbers the OCR misread were corrected from the page image. Every published row was read against the page image, location first; a cost or name not legible on the image, or past a column or page break, was left out, and where the printed total and the printed instalments disagree no cost is given. Owners who are private individuals are never recorded, nor is a contractor or architect who is the owner, shares the owner's surname, or is listed at the owner's premises; sureties are cut. Held back at the image (54 of 205): minor work such as signs, small repairs and partitions (17), storey, unit or use counts that contradict the roll (13), small alterations and plain single houses on parcels with no page (11, held for a page), contracts the page already carries in full from the San Francisco Call (7), entries cut off by a page break or with no legible description (2), a row of four houses on one listing, two contracts for the lodging house at Geary and Jones because the page credits another architect for the building on the parcel that corner resolves to, and one contract placed on a parcel with no sf-eas-addresses row. check.py --overlap: 40 of the picked rows were on pages that already carry a Call entry of the same week (the 1906-1913 newspaper recovery). Seven were dropped as above; nineteen were trimmed to what this paper adds (the architect, the contractor or the price); the rest are different contracts for the same building or were kept whole because the Call entry names no one or gives a different price (430 Twenty-eighth Avenue: $3,600 on the page image here, $3,000 in the Call entry). The permit of 20 May for one-storey brick stores at Geary and Mason (C. Withers) is published as a record only; the building the page describes is the two-storey cafe building contracted in October 1913, and its credits were left alone. One held fact of the later run (1485 Church Street, 19 May 1920) was read against its page image and taken up when this volume seeded the page.

coverage.remaining: All eight half-year volumes on the Internet Archive are read. In this volume: 151 rows placed on a parcel whose roll year fits, single houses with no architect named and no page, are logged and held until another fact gives the parcel a page (extra.placed_apn; they still need the image check), and 11 more were held for a page at the image. 709 rows were not placed: location lines not parsed (tract lots, garbled headings), street pairs that do not cross under the names read, and printed street numbers with no EAS row today. The rest have a nearest parcel that was not accepted.
coverage.note: 2,547 numbered entries read, 1,494 San Francisco rows, 785 placed on a parcel, 205 picked and read against the page image, 151 published on 139 pages (46 seeded), 54 held back at the image.
